questions.q: What does the hue argument do in a seaborn function such as scatterplot?
options: Sets the resolution of the saved image
Splits the data by a category column, coloring each group and adding a legend
Chooses the font of the axis labels
Sorts the DataFrame before plotting
questions.explain: hue names a column whose categories are mapped to colors, so groups can be compared on a single chart.

questions.q: How does seaborn relate to matplotlib?
options: It replaces matplotlib entirely
It draws onto matplotlib axes, so fig, ax and savefig still apply
It only works in the R language
It can only make interactive charts
questions.explain: seaborn is built on matplotlib. Its functions accept an ax= argument and produce matplotlib figures you can customize and save.

questions.q: Which seaborn function would you use to compare the spread of spend across customer segments?
options: heatmap
pairplot
lineplot
boxplot
questions.explain: A box plot shows median, quartiles and outliers for each group, which is ideal for comparing distributions across categories.

questions.q: In sns.heatmap(corr, annot=True, cmap="coolwarm", vmin=-1, vmax=1), what does annot=True do?
options: Adds an annotation arrow to the highest value
Sorts the correlations from highest to lowest
Writes each cell's numeric value inside the cell
Converts the heatmap to a bar chart
questions.explain: annot=True prints each correlation on its cell. The diverging coolwarm palette with vmin=-1 and vmax=1 centers the color scale on zero.

questions.q: What does sns.pairplot(customers, hue="segment") give you?
options: A scatter plot for every pair of numeric columns, with distributions on the diagonal, colored by segment
A single pie chart of the segments
A statistical test comparing the segments
A table of summary statistics
questions.explain: pairplot draws a grid of pairwise scatter plots plus a distribution for each variable, a quick overview of a table with a few numeric columns.
